propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Ecclesiam tuam, Domine, miseratio continuata mundet et muniat: et quia sine
te non potest salva consistere; tuo semper munere gubernetur. Per Dominum.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 428 (running head `XV. SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST.`) under `COLLECT. Ecclesiam.` after the Introit `Inclina, Domine`, which begins under the heading `XV. SUNDAY after PENTECOST.` on p. 427. The printed Latin cue Ecclesiam. and the English petition answer the target Ecclesiam tuam, Domine. Read again from the exact registered PDF at 200 and 400 dpi on 2026-10-01; its SHA-256 was independently checked. This is the pre-1955 lay hand-missal English witness, not a modern approved liturgical translation.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: May thy continual mercy purify and defend thy church: and since without thee it cannot be safe, may it always be directed by the influence of thy grace. Thro'.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Tua nos, Domine, sacramenta custodiant: et contra diabolicos semper tueantur
incursus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Printed p. 429 (running head `XVI. SUNDAY AFTER PENTECOST.`) under `SECRET.—` with no Latin cue, after the Offertory `Ps. xxxix.`; the page prints no conclusion. The book prints one Secret here, as the 1962 formulary has one. Its position before the Communion within Sunday XV and the clauses for the mysteries preserving us against the devil answer Tua nos, Domine, sacramenta custodiant ... contra diabolicos ... incursus. The lack of an English conclusion is a property of this historical witness, not an instruction to shorten the 1962 Latin. Read again from the exact registered PDF at 200 and 400 dpi on 2026-10-01; its SHA-256 was independently checked. This is the pre-1955 lay hand-missal English witness, not a modern approved liturgical translation.
translations.source_label: The Roman Missal translated into the English language for the use of the laity, first revised edition (Philadelphia: Eugene Cummiskey, 1861)
translations.text: May thy mysteries, O Lord, preserve us, and always defend us against the attacks of the devil.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Mentes nostras et corpora possideat, quaesumus, Domine, doni caelestis
operatio: ut non noster sensus in nobis, sed jugiter ejus praeveniat
effectus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit
et regnat in unitate.

The printed Latin cue Mentes. and the English petition answer the target Mentes nostras. Read again from the exact registered PDF at 200 and 400 dpi on 2026-10-01; its SHA-256 was independently checked.
